record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Is being an even real Banach space a 3-space property, meaning that whenever a closed subspace and the corresponding quotient space have the property, the whole Banach space must have the property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real Banach space $X$ is called even if it is isomorphic to its square $X \oplus X$. A property $\mathcal{P}$ of Banach spaces is called a 3-space property if, whenever a Banach space $Z$ contains a closed subspace $Y$ such that both $Y$ and the quotient $Z/Y$ have property $\mathcal{P}$, then $Z$ itself has property $\mathcal{P}$.

Determine whether the property of being even is a 3-space property. That is, decide whether the following implication holds for every short exact sequence of real Banach spaces
$$0 \longrightarrow Y \longrightarrow Z \longrightarrow Z/Y \longrightarrow 0:$$
if $Y \cong Y \oplus Y$ and $Z/Y \cong (Z/Y) \oplus (Z/Y)$, then $Z \cong Z \oplus Z$.

A web search did not surface a published resolution of whether evenness (being isomorphic to one's square) is a 3-space property; the status appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive recent reference confirming "still open" was located.
